text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a practice where developers regularly merge their code into a shared repository. Each time code is added, automated builds start and tests run automatically. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious problems. A CI pipeline usually includes steps such as building the project, running unit tests, and checking code quality. When a test fails, the team gets quick feedback and can fix the problem immediately. This makes the development process faster and more reliable, and it reduces the risk of bugs reaching production.
